text.tspan: Share of warm-season deaths attributed to heat in a world with and
The "warm season" varies by country, but typically lasts 3 to 5 months of the year. Shown is the share of premature deaths
in this season that can be attributed to heat, with the natural climate and extra warming from human-induced climate
change. Based on data over the period from 1991 to 2018.

tspan.tspan: Vicedo-Cabrera et al. (2021). The burden of heat-related mortality attributable to recent human-induced climate change. Nature
